chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both)

That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on a rainy night would delay the Maghrib prayer and hasten the 'Isha prayer, so he would pray both of them together, and he would say, 'He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.'

key_terms.مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمْ لاَ يُرْحَمْ: He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining prayers during rain according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) practical application of *jam' taqdim* (combining prayers) during rain, a practice later codified in Shia fiqh as a concession (*rukhsa*) to prevent hardship. By delaying Maghrib to allow congregants to arrive and hastening 'Isha, he embodied the principle of *rahmah* (mercy), linking physical ease with spiritual compassion as affirmed by his closing phrase. This establishes a precedent for prioritizing communal welfare and ease in ritual observance, a key theme in Usuli jurisprudence.
